questions.question: Which material-specific PL enhancement factors did the authors report after paraffin coating, in the order MoS₂, WS₂, WSe₂, and MoSe₂?
questions.rationale: The reported factors depend on material and starting flake; MoS₂ showed the largest enhancement, while WSe₂ had the smallest.
questions.evidence_quote: MoS 2 , WS 2 , WSe 2 , and MoSe 2 show factors of enhancement of 215-, 55-, 9-, and 50-fold from the as-exfoliated flakes, respectively.

questions.question: What coating-related spectral change did the authors interpret as evidence for reduced carrier concentration and more exciton-dominated emission?

options.A: A narrower PL FWHM and an upshift of the PL peak after coating
options.B: A broader PL FWHM and a redshift of the PL peak after coating
options.C: An unchanged FWHM with a larger low-energy trion shoulder
options.D: A Raman E′ upshift and A′ downshift without a PL peak shift

questions.rationale: They interpret decreased FWHM and a peak upshift after paraffin coating as a decrease in carrier number and greater exciton-derived PL.
questions.evidence_quote: The decrease in the FWHM and the upshift of the peak suggest that the number of carriers in the monolayer TMDCs would decrease, and the PL spectra after paraffin coating is dominated by exciton-derived emission

questions.question: How did the authors prepare paraffin for spin coating, and why was a heat blower used during coating?

options.A: They melted it at 80 °C and used a heat blower to prevent immediate solidification during spin coating
options.B: They dissolved it at 42–45 °C and used a blower to evaporate the solvent after coating
options.C: They melted it at 120 °C and cooled the sample to crystallize a transparent film
options.D: They applied it below its melting point and used the blower to induce substrate desorption

questions.rationale: Paraffin melts at 42–45 °C, was pre-melted at 80 °C, and a hair-dryer heat blower kept it molten while spin-coating.
questions.evidence_quote: The paraffin used in this research has a melting point of 42-45 °C. For paraffin coating, the paraffin was melted on a hot plate at 80 °C in advance and dropped onto a sample placed on a spin coater

questions.question: What time-dependent sequence was shown for an unconfined monolayer MoS₂ after paraffin coating?

options.A: Images were taken as-exfoliated, immediately after coating, after 2 h, and after a further 1 h; the monolayer deformed while nearby bulk flakes retained their shape
options.B: Images were taken after 1, 2, and 3 days; both monolayer and bulk flakes slowly dissolved
options.C: Images were taken immediately and after 30 min; paraffin prevented any shape change in the monolayer
options.D: Images were taken at 60, 80, 100, and 120 °C; the substrate heated uniformly and flattened the flake

questions.rationale: The microscopy sequence follows the spontaneous deformation over the first three hours at room temperature; surrounding bulk material remains morphologically stable.
questions.evidence_quote: The monolayer MoS 2 deformed spontaneously with time, while the surrounding bulk flakes maintained their morphology.

questions.question: What opposite Raman shifts were observed for monolayer MoS₂ after paraffin treatment, and what did the authors infer from them?

options.A: E′ shifted −0.72 cm⁻¹ on average, indicating strain; A′ shifted +1.03 cm⁻¹, indicating decreased carrier concentration
options.B: E′ shifted +1.03 cm⁻¹, indicating strain; A′ shifted −0.72 cm⁻¹, indicating increased carrier concentration
options.C: Both E′ and A′ shifted −0.72 cm⁻¹, indicating complete strain relaxation
options.D: Both peaks shifted +1.03 cm⁻¹, indicating increased substrate electron doping

questions.rationale: The in-plane E′ mode shifts negatively while the out-of-plane A′ mode shifts positively; the paper associates these with strain and reduced carrier concentration, respectively.
questions.evidence_quote: The Eʹ peak shifted in the negative direction after paraffin coating by about -0.72 cm -1 on average (Table 2 ), indicating the strain inside the monolayer MoS 2 .

questions.question: For a monolayer MoS₂ laterally constrained by bulk flakes on three sides, how did the spatial PL signal vary after coating?

options.A: The center intensity was about 2.3 times the rim, and the center PL peak was 5–10 meV lower in energy
options.B: The rim intensity was 2.3 times the center, and the center peak was 5–10 meV higher in energy
options.C: The center intensity was uniform with the rim, while the peak shifted 50 meV higher
options.D: The center intensity was 9 times the rim, with no measurable peak-position difference

questions.rationale: The confined flake showed a brighter center and a modest redshift there, consistent with a spatially varying strain state.
questions.evidence_quote: the intensity is about 2.3 times greater in the center than at the rim.

questions.question: What two coupled physical effects did the authors propose as the origin of the PL enhancement?

options.A: Strain from paraffin's large thermal-expansion-driven volume change and subsequent partial monolayer desorption from the substrate
options.B: Charge transfer from paraffin and permanent creation of sulfur vacancies
options.C: Chemical p-doping by paraffin and complete removal of all wrinkles
options.D: Thermal annealing of the substrate and increased electron transfer into the monolayer

questions.rationale: The proposed mechanism combines mechanical strain generated by paraffin volume change with local separation of the monolayer from the substrate, reducing substrate effects.
questions.evidence_quote: PL enhancement in monolayer TMDCs is due to a combination of two effects: strain induced by the volume change caused by the high thermal expansion coefficient of the paraffin and the subsequent desorption of the monolayer TMDC flakes from the substrate.

questions.question: How did the PL mapping of the monolayer surrounded by bulk flakes differ from the full desorption/bundling case?

options.A: Large bending and bundling were constrained, but in-plane fluctuations could still create a wrinkle and partial local desorption
options.B: The bulk flakes increased the paraffin expansion coefficient, causing more severe complete bundling
options.C: The monolayer remained perfectly flat and could not show local PL enhancement
options.D: The surrounding bulk flakes chemically passivated the monolayer and eliminated substrate effects uniformly

questions.rationale: Bulk flakes mechanically prevent large deformation, but paraffin shrinkage can still strain the monolayer plane and generate a local wrinkle where partial substrate separation occurs.
questions.evidence_quote: In the case of monolayer MoS 2 surrounded by bulk flakes on three sides, large deformation is prevented, but the fluctuation of the monolayer in the plane may happen due to mechanical stress caused by the volume shrinkage of the paraffin throughout the process

questions.question: Which limitation did the authors note for a thick paraffin film made by simple casting rather than spin coating?

options.A: It appeared glassy and was not transparent
options.B: It became electrically conductive and quenched all PL
options.C: It failed to cover the entire monolayer surface
options.D: It melted at room temperature and could not be examined optically

questions.rationale: Spin-coated paraffin formed a transparent film, whereas a thick simply cast film had a glassy, opaque appearance.
questions.evidence_quote: A thick film of paraffin achieved by simple casting, not by spin coating, resulted in a glassy appearance that was not transparent.

questions.question: Why did the authors argue that paraffin coating provides a broader strategy than sulfur-TMDC-focused treatments such as TFSI?

options.A: It enhanced PL in both sulfur- and selenium-based monolayers, including WSe₂, for which prior strategies were limited
options.B: It selectively enhanced sulfur compounds while suppressing selenium-compound emission
options.C: It replaced all chemical treatment methods by permanently doping only MoS₂
options.D: It enhanced PL only after transferring every monolayer to quartz substrates

questions.rationale: The paper demonstrates application to MoS₂, WS₂, MoSe₂, and WSe₂, unlike several prior chemical treatments that were ineffective for selenium-based materials.
questions.evidence_quote: This result suggests that paraffin film formation is widely applicable in both sulfur-and selenium-based TMDCs.
